NCVBDC2023.publisher: National Center for Vector Borne Diseases Control (NCVBDC), DGHS, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India
NCVBDC2023.note: Section numbers follow the printed chapter and section headings (e.g. 4.1, Box 2, 7.1).

WHO2009.title: Dengue: guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, prevention and control
WHO2009.note: 2009 edition, file 9789241547871_eng.pdf. Section numbers follow the printed headings (e.g. 2.3.2.1, Textbox C).

CDC_POCKET.title: Dengue Case Management (pocket guide)
CDC_POCKET.publisher: [CITATION NEEDED: confirm publisher. File 20240521_342849-B_PRESS_READY_PocketGuideDCMC_UPDATE.pdf, PubID 301358; its text credits the 2022 PAHO guidelines and Paz-Bailey et al., Lancet 2024.]
CDC_POCKET.note: Cited by printed page number (p.1 to p.8).

recentFeverDays.note: Spec 5.3 says "fever (current or within 7 days)". Compared with whole days since the onset date.

sourceRefs.note: critical phase "usually on days 3-7 of illness"
children: between 3-7 days of onset of fever
after the 3rd or 4th day of fever
persistent vomiting = 3 episodes in 1 hr or 4 in 6 hrs

vomitingEpisodes24h.note: Spec 5.3 gives N=3 per 24 h as a placeholder. The pocket guide defines it differently (3 in 1 hour or 4 in 6 hours). Doctor must choose; the spec value is the more sensitive one.

sourceRefs.note: platelets below 100,000 may be seen in dengue

plateletEmergency.note: NOT found in the sources as a "go to hospital now" cut-off. Doctor to confirm or replace.

sourceRefs.note: drop below 100,000 per microlitre may be observed in dengue
antiplatelet drugs may be stopped when platelets are below one lakh

plateletSeeDoctor.note: NOT found in the sources as a "see a doctor today" cut-off. Doctor to confirm or replace.

plateletRapidFallFraction.note: UNSET ON PURPOSE: the sources say "rapid" without a number and the spec gives none. The rule that uses it is inert until a doctor supplies a value, and the protocol cannot be REVIEWED while it is null.

sourceRefs.note: a rising haematocrit of 10% above baseline is an early objective indicator of plasma leakage

hematocritRiseFraction.note: Treated as a relative rise versus the previous reading. Doctor to confirm relative vs absolute and the baseline definition.

sourceRefs.note: severe dengue: AST or ALT of 1000 U/L (comparison symbol is not legible in the extracted text; treated as greater-or-equal)

transaminaseSevere.note: Doctor to confirm greater-than vs greater-or-equal.

infantAgeMonths.note: Spec 5.3: infant under 12 months with any fever.

sourceRefs.note: infants and children (age <10 years) especially with malnutrition

childAgeMonths.note: Spec 5.3 uses age under 5 years. The NCVBDC high-risk list says under 10 years with malnutrition. Doctor to decide.

elderAgeMonths.note: Spec says age 65 or older; sources say over 65. Doctor to confirm.

sourceRefs.note: CBC for all patients with fever >3 days

riskFeverDays.note: Spec 5.3: fever 3 days or more with any risk factor.

riskFloorFeverDays.note: Spec 5.4: floor at SEE_DOCTOR_TODAY when fever persists 2 days or more with a risk factor.

sourceRefs.note: NS1 for samples collected from day 1 to 5 and IgM after 5 days
CBC for all patients with warning signs and all with fever >3 days
intolerance to oral administration of fluids

dangerSigns.note: Sign is sourced; the count that defines "persistent" is a spec placeholder (see threshold).
Not asked when sex is male (applicableWhen).

sourceRefs.note: pass urine at least once every six hours; bring to hospital if not passing urine for more than 4-6 hours

dangerSigns.note: WHO supports the 6 hour window used by the spec; NCVBDC PHC advice says 12 hours. The 6 hour window is fixed by the question wording.

sourceRefs.note: hepatitis / hepatic failure as organ dysfunction

dangerSigns.note: Jaundice itself is listed in the spec; the sources describe liver involvement rather than jaundice.
Spec 5.4 names this sign but gives no level. Treated as EMERGENCY_NOW (cautious). Doctor to decide.

noFeverDangerSign.note: Spec is silent on danger signs without fever. HOME_CARE requires no matching symptoms, so this never stays at HOME_CARE.

unknownEmergencyRule.note: Spec 5.1 unknown_is_emergency list: can keep fluids down; drowsy/confused; bleeding. Reason ids are UNKNOWN_EMERGENCY:<signId>. The "when" field is unused for this rule.

uncertainDanger.note: Spec 5.1: UNKNOWN raises urgency, capped at SEE_DOCTOR_TODAY. Reason ids are UNCERTAIN_DANGER:<signId>. The "when" field is unused for this rule.

sourceRefs.note: haemolytic diseases such as G6PD deficiency, thalassaemia and other haemoglobinopathies

riskFactors.note: Added beyond the spec list because all three sources name it. Doctor to confirm.

sourceRefs.note: patients on anti-platelet or anticoagulant medications should be carefully monitored
living alone or far from a health facility without reliable transport

stepUpRule.note: Spec 5.4 says raise one step. Capped at SEE_DOCTOR_TODAY so it agrees with spec 5.3 (fever 3 days or more with a risk factor is SEE_DOCTOR_TODAY, not EMERGENCY_NOW). Only danger signs can reach EMERGENCY_NOW. Doctor to confirm.

sourceRefs.note: warning signs usually occur near the end of the febrile phase, at defervescence
recognise the critical phase that follows defervescence

rules.note: Redundant with the individual sign rules by design: it adds the explanation.
Cut-off is a spec placeholder (see threshold).

sourceRefs.note: rapid fall of platelet count may indicate progression

rules.note: INERT until plateletRapidFallFraction is set by a doctor.

sourceRefs.note: progressive increase in haematocrit with a rapid decrease in platelet count

rules.note: "Falling" here means any decrease; "rapid" is not quantified in the sources.
Cut-off is a spec placeholder (see threshold).

sourceRefs.note: clinical description: headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia, arthralgia, rash
IV fluids needed with poor oral intake
refusal to take orally / poor intake
NSAIDs may aggravate gastritis or bleeding

rules.note: An unsure answer about painkillers counts as "took one" (cautious).

sourceRefs.note: decrease in urination; check number of wet diapers

rules.note: Contradictory or malformed input never lowers urgency (spec 2.3).

sourceRefs.note: probable dengue: compatible illness during an outbreak
duration of fever assessed at triage

rules.note: Spec is silent. A positive test never leaves the result at HOME_CARE_WITH_TRIGGERS.

sourceRefs.note: mention day of onset of fever and day of sample collection
